## Empirical anchor

2026-05-13 surfaced by PRINCIPAL during the substrate-architecture discussion:

> "We also have whatever long term way that the user's agents have to store memories about them and their work. For example, you have a pretty large set of memories about me and some specific to ariadne and the stoa or broad memories about my preferences that shape your output. We need to treat this as a feature and not a problem that each user will be unique and their agents will interpret the same inputs differently. This will help our agentic teams align with the user's goals."

## The principle

User-tier and project-tier memories are the **user-alignment layer** of the agent identity. Different users → different memory accumulations → different agent behaviors. This is the alignment mechanism working correctly, not noise to normalize away.

A Stoa-team-deployed agent's identity has four layers:

| Layer | Content | Variance |
|---|---|---|
| Role file | What kind of agent (POLYBIUS / PLINY / CAPTAIN_X) | Universal across users |
| Memories | Standing user preferences, accumulated lessons, project-specific knowledge | **Unique per user / project** |
| Handoff | Current work-state for session continuity | Unique per engagement |
| bw substrate | Durable detail (tickets, history, comments) | Unique per project |

The role file is the same for every deployment; the memories are what make the agent serve THIS user effectively. Substrate should support memory accumulation as a first-class feature, not paper over it.

## The substrate-canon shape

Document the principle in operating-disciplines.md (likely as a section paired with the two-team-pattern + semi-persistence sections):

- The four-layer identity model
- Memories as the user-alignment layer (not noise to normalize)
- Memory introspection should be easy + supported ("what do you remember about me?" returns clean answer)
- Memory authoring is collaborative (user correction + expansion as a normal action)
- Memories travel with agent identity (persist across compactions, project team modifications, etc.)
- When the base team designs the project team, the project team inherits memory-access conventions

## Substrate touch-points

- `substrate/operating-disciplines.md` — new section on memory-as-alignment-feature
- `substrate/MAJOR_POLYBIUS.md` — discipline note: POLYBIUS treats user memories as authoritative for user-alignment
- `substrate/MAJOR_PLINY.md` — analogous discipline note
- Possibly: a substrate-tier `memory-introspect` skill — agents load it when user asks "what do you remember?" — returns curated memory index

## Gauntlet

DAEDALUS-light + ADA + CATO. Substrate-prose edit. ~60-100 LOC across op-disc + 2 role files. Possibly +1 light skill if memory-introspect is in scope.

## Sequencing

P2. Arc 25 candidate. Bundles with two-team-pattern + multi-team-pattern + operating-mode-progression + handoff-author skill.

## Cross-references

- `stoa--7e3` — handoff-author skill (handoffs reference memories per principle 5: "cite, don't duplicate")
- Two-team-pattern ticket — base team and project team both have their own memory accumulation
- The accumulated user-tier memory at `~/.claude/CLAUDE.md` + project-tier memories — the empirical anchor for what memory-accumulation looks like in practice
title: Substrate canon: memories as the user-alignment layer (feature, not noise)
